home.why4Desc: Referral campaigns and links change. We review them regularly to reduce the chance of sending you to outdated or weaker offers.
home.comparisonTitle: See which exchange is actually cheaper

home.personaTitle: Pick by how you actually trade
home.personaSubtitle: The best exchange depends on your goal, not just on the highest headline rebate.
home.persona1Desc: New to crypto? Start with platforms that are easier to learn, more complete in products, and friendlier for first-time users.
home.persona2Desc: If you care about depth, slippage, and tooling, these exchanges fit active derivatives traders better.
home.persona3Desc: If your priority is long-term fee recovery, compare rebate rates together with the underlying trading fee structure.
home.persona4Desc: If you chase new and long-tail tokens, focus on listing breadth, smaller-market liquidity, and rebate terms together.
home.faq1A: An exchange rebate means part of the trading fees you pay is returned to your account under the exchange's referral rules. Register through CryptoRebate and you can keep receiving that fee cashback.
home.faq2Q: Does using a rebate link cost extra?
home.faq2A: No. In normal cases, using a rebate link does not increase your trading fees, and some exchanges may also provide extra discounts. The rebate comes from the exchange's marketing budget, not from an extra fee charged to you.
home.faq3A: Settlement depends on the exchange. Common patterns are instant rebate credit or daily settlement. Always check the current campaign rules on the exchange page.
home.faq4A: We currently focus on Binance, OKX, Bybit, Bitget, Gate.io, KuCoin, and Huobi (HTX), with more exchanges and refreshed offers added over time.

about.title: What Are Crypto Exchange Rebates?
about.subtitle: Understand what a rebate is, how it settles, and why it usually does not add cost before you decide to register through a referral link.
about.whatDesc: When you trade on an exchange, you pay spot or futures fees. Some exchanges allow part of those fees to be returned to you through a referral relationship — that is the rebate. CryptoRebate exists to organize those offers, fee structures, and signup links clearly before you choose where to register.
about.step1: Register on an exchange through CryptoRebate's link
about.step2: Trade crypto as you normally would
about.step3: The exchange automatically returns part of your fees
about.step4: Rebates are deposited directly to your exchange account
about.costDesc: Usually no. Registering through a rebate link does not normally increase the base trading fee you pay to the exchange; the cashback comes from the exchange's referral or marketing budget. What matters more is whether the rebate activates automatically, how it settles, and whether the base fee is competitive in the first place.
about.riskDesc: CryptoRebate provides exchange rebate information, comparisons, and signup links. We do not provide investment advice, and a rebate does not reduce market risk, liquidation risk, or platform risk. It only lowers part of your fee drag if the exchange offer remains valid.
about.faq1Q: What's the difference between rebates and fee discounts?
about.faq1A: Fee discounts directly reduce your trading rate. Rebates return a portion of fees after trading. Both save you money, and some exchanges offer both.
about.faq2Q: Will rebates affect my trading experience?
about.faq2A: No. After registering through a rebate link, your trading experience is identical to direct registration with all features available.
about.faq3Q: I already have an exchange account. Can I still get rebates?
about.faq3A: Usually a new account is needed to bind the rebate relationship. Consider registering with a new email. Some exchanges support binding referral codes to existing accounts — check each exchange's rules.

disclosure.howWeEarnDesc: CryptoRebate earns revenue through affiliate or referral partnerships. When a user registers through a link we publish and later trades under the exchange's campaign rules, we may receive commission from that exchange.
disclosure.noCostDesc: That commission is typically paid from the exchange's existing marketing or referral budget, not by adding an extra fee on top of your trading cost. Your real cost still depends on base fees, rebate rate, rebate activation, and whether token discounts can stack.
